D.treatment: presentation of the pedagogical design principles

O.outcome_detail: participants' agreement that the principles foster learning and motivation towards STEM

result.effect: 94.34% agreed or strongly agreed; 50% agreed and 44.34% strongly agreed

cells.quote: In focus group 2, after presenting the pedagogical framework created based on the feedback from focus group 1, 94.34% of all the participants (n = 137) in focus group 2 either agreed (50%) or strongly agreed (44.34%) with the statement, “the presented pedagogical design principles foster learning and motivation towards STEM”.
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive member-check survey, not a treatment-versus-comparison experiment. The comparison is therefore only the remaining disagree/strongly-disagree responses, and no inferential test, confidence interval, or adequate-power claim is reported.

O.outcome_detail: parental involvement as perceived by students

cells.quote: At the end of the first year, the intervention show ed to be effective on four outcomes: it increased parental involvement (as perceived by stu dents), it reduced their perception of teachers’ hostility and it improved their self-effi cacy about learning and improved their satisfaction about their school experience. All the se effects are statistically and substantially significant (p-value< 0.05 and effect size>.20).
cells.note: The study reports individual-level random assignment of 131 students to treatment and 131 to control; only 84 assigned treatment students accepted the intervention.

cells.quote: The training programs produced meaningful impacts at both organizational and individual levels. Organizationally, the training contributed to the validation of infectious disease response protocols, strengthen interdepartmental collaboration, and the establishment of safer working environments. Individually, participants reported improved response competencies, enhanced professional knowledge, greater psychological stability, and the development of innovative perspectives on infectious disease management.
cells.note: Participants reported perceived improvements, but the study did not use a quantitative pre-post comparison or report an effect size.

cells.quote: One program that stayed with me was the mock emergency drill at the National Medical Center, where we had to wear PPE and respond to a simulated emergency. Repeating the donning and doffing helped reduce my anxiety little by little.

O.outcome_detail: field readiness and infectious-disease response competency

cells.quote: These findings highlight the importance of shifting from theory-based to practice-oriented education on infectious disease responses. To build sustainable preparedness systems, training programs should be scenario-driven, repetitive, and psychologically supportive.
cells.note: The contrast is a qualitative recommendation grounded in participant reports and perceived needs, not an experimental comparison.

O.outcome_detail: response competence and applicability to real-world scenarios

cells.quote: Instructional methods were primarily practice-oriented, featuring simulations, mock drills, case-based learning, and hands-on sessions, which participants found highly applicable to real-world scenarios.
cells.note: The contrast with theory-based training is stated in the study's conclusion and discussion of barriers, but outcomes were based on participant perceptions rather than a controlled comparison.

cells.note: This is a participant's perceived effect of repeated practice; no quantitative effect size or controlled comparison was reported.
